levels.title: Look at the smallest inputs
levels.body_md: Your idea works for most weights. Try the smallest values of w one by one and split them by hand.
levels.question_back: For each small w, what are the two parts exactly?

levels.title: Both parts must be positive
levels.body_md: Being even is not enough on its own: each of the two parts must be even AND greater than zero. Some even weight cannot be split that way.
levels.question_back: Which even w has no split into two positive even parts?

levels.title: Line 6 accepts w = 2
levels.body_md: On line 6 you print `YES` for every even `w`. For `w = 2` the only split is `1 + 1`, so the correct answer is `NO`, but your program prints `YES` (verified by running your code).

levels.title: Even and bigger than two
levels.body_md: An even w ≥ 4 can always be split as 2 + (w − 2), and both parts are even and positive. An odd w can never be split into two even parts, and w = 2 only splits into 1 + 1. So the answer is YES exactly when w is even and w > 2. Change the condition on line 6 to also require w > 2. Time complexity stays O(1).
